Tatpur. 1

. m. f. n. (-ब्जः-ब्जा-ब्जम्) Born or produced
in, or by, water.
2. m. (-ब्जः)
 ^1 The moon.
 ^2 Dhanwantari, the physi-
cian of the gods (he having arisen from the ocean when it
was churned for the amṛta).
 ^3 A fish.
 ^4 The ratan (Calamus
rotang).
 ^5 The name of two other aquatic plants:
 a. Valisneria
octandra;
 b. Barringtonia acutangula.
 ^6 The proper name of
the father of Viśala; see also अब्जककुभ.
 ^7 (In Arithmetic
sometimes used to denote) the numeral 1. Comp. चन्द्र.
3. m. n. (-ब्जः-ब्जम्) The conch.
4. n. (-ब्जम्)
 ^1 A lotus; (according to the Sārasvatā-
bhidhāna the white esculent variety; ‘पङ्कजकैरवे’).
 ^2 A
large number, a million of millions; Līlavatī: एकदशशत-
सहस्रायुतलक्षप्रयुतकोटयः क्रमशः । अर्बुदमब्जं खर्वनिखर्वम-
हापद्मशङ्कवस्तस्मात् । जलधिश्चान्त्यं मध्यं परार्धमिति दशगु-
णोत्तराः संज्ञाः । संख्यायाः स्थानानां व्यवहारार्थं कृताः पूर्वैः.
 ^3 A sort of collyrium; see रसाञ्जन.

5. f. (-ब्जा) A pearl oyster. [The meanings

. 5. a.,
4. 3. and 5. are given in Sureśvara's Śabdapratīpa, where
the word is thus defined: अब्जं रसाञ्जने पद्मे स्त्रियां शुक्तौ
च पुंसि च । शङ्खशैवलमत्स्येषु वेतसे रजनीकरे.] Compare
अब्जा. E. अप् and ज.
अब्जा
Tatpur. 1

. m. (-ब्जाः)
 ^1 Born or produced, in, or by,
water; a vaidik epithet of Fire (see अहि and comp. अप्),
and of Āditya or the Sun in the type Dadhikrā, when he
is identified with Parabrahman or the universal deity, ac-
cording to Sāyaṇa, because the Sun is born in the midst
of the water; according to Mahīdhara, because he has
horses which are born from the waters, or as the Aitareya
Brāhmaṇa intimates, on account of the Sun's apparent ris-
ing from the ocean and setting in the same (see Wilson's
Ṛgveda vol. 3, p. 200 note).
 ^2 A lotus.
 ^3 The moon.
2. f. (-ब्जाः) Lakṣmī or Śrī. [The last three meanings
are given by the Śabdaratnāvalī where the two E. I. H.
Mss., 1512 and 1585, refer the name of Śrī to the masc.;
[]
both words अब्ज and अब्जा are thus explained: अब्जः शङ्खे
स्त्रियां (which must be read ऽस्त्रियां) ना तु धन्वन्तर्यम्बुजे
त्रिषु । क्लीवं पद्मे तथाब्जास्तु पद्मेन्दुश्रीष्वसौ पुमान्; there
seems to be no incorrectness in the text of the Mss., for
Mathureśa takes now and then the liberties of a verse-
maker, but a male Śrī appears nevertheless to be a stronger
license even than a curtailed धन्वन्तृ (loc. धन्वन्तरि) instead
of धन्वन्तरि (loc. धन्वन्तरौ).] E. अप् and जा (जन्, kṛt aff. विट्).

अब्जककुभ Dwandwa m. pl. (-भाः) The descendants of Abja
and of Kakubha; (the patronymic affix is dropped in this
compound; otherwise the descendants of अब्ज would be
आब्जयः and those of ककुभ, काकुभाः; the word itself is
the reading of, and explained by, the Kāśikā (E. I.

)
in the Gaṇa to Pāṇ.

.; the present edition of Pāṇ. and
the E. I. H. Ms. of the
Kāś. 829

read उब्जककुभाः). E. अब्ज
(instead of आब्जि q. v.) and ककुभ (instead of काकुभ q. v.).

अब्जकर्णिका Tatpur. f. (-का) The seed vessel of a lotus (= कम-
लवीजकोशः). Comp. अम्भोरुहकर्णिका. E. अब्ज and कर्णिका.

अब्जज Tatpur. m. (-जः) A name of (the masc.) Brahman;
(the god having sprung at the creation from the lotus which
arose from the navel of Viṣṇu). Comp. अब्जयोनि. E. अब्ज
and ज.

अब्जदृश् Bahuvr. m. f. n. (-क्-क्-क्) Lotus-eyed, having
large fine eyes. E. अब्ज and दृश्.

अब्जनयन Bahuvr. m. f. n. (-नः-ना-नम्) The same as अब्ज-
दृश्. E. अब्ज and नयन.

अब्जनेत्र Bahuvr. m. f. n. (-त्रः-त्रा-त्रम्) The same as अब्ज-
दृश्. E. अब्ज and नेत्र.

अब्जबान्धव Tatpur. m. (-वः) The sun; comp. पद्मबन्धु and
अब्जिनीपति. E. अब्ज and बान्धव; ‘the friend of the lotus’.

अब्जभोग Tatpur. m. (-गः) The root of the lotus. E. अब्ज
and भोग.

अब्जयोनि Bahuvr. m. (-निः) A name of (the masc.) Bra-
hman; comp. अब्जज. E. अब्ज and योनि.

अब्जवाहन Tatpur. m. (-नः) A name of Śiva; (the god being
the vehicle of, i. e. carrying, the moon on his forehead).
E. अब्ज and वाहन.

अब्जवीजभृत् Tatpur. m. (-त्) The white variety of Oleander
or Nerium odorum; see करवीर. E. अब्ज-वीज and भृत्.

अब्जस् n. (-ब्जः) Form, shape, beauty. E. आप् with the vowel
shortened, uṇ. aff. असुन्, āgama जुट्; (but more probably
a Tatpur. of अप् in the sense of अपस् ‘work’,--comp.
अप्सस्--and जस् from जन्).

अब्जहस्त Bahuvr. m. (-स्तः) The sun; (Sūrya is represented
when sitting on his chariot, holding a lotus in one hand).
E. अब्ज and हस्त.

अब्जाह्व Bahuvr. m. (?) (-ह्वः) A grass the roots of which are
fragrant and are used for tatties &c. (Andropogon murica-
tum). E. अब्ज and आह्वा.

अब्जित् Tatpur. m. (-त्) The conqueror of the waters; a
vaidik epithet of Indra, because he conquers the waters
attacked by Vṛtra. E. अप् and जित्.

अब्जिनी f. (-नी) A place abounding in lotus flowers. (The ex-
planations of नलिनी by Bharata, as quoted also by Rādhā-
kāntad., viz. an assemblage of lotus flowers, a place abound-
ing in lotus flowers and the flexible stalk of a lotus, do
not necessarily apply, more especially the last, to अब्जिनी.)
E. अब्ज, taddh. aff. इनि.

अब्जिनीपति Tatpur. m. (-तिः) The sun. (Comp. अब्जबान्धव.
E. अब्जिनी and पति.
